$comment: Example configuration for scripts/cogload-dashboard.py.
Copy to your repository root as cogload.config.json and edit.
Every field is optional: with no config at all the tool probes the local git tree.
The three lanes are the framework and are fixed; probes are what you plug in.
lane 1 Verify    — needs a human decision (fed by decision_queue, not by probes)
lane 2 Integrate — live-measured state you must reconcile
lane 3 Steward   — policy, discipline and cost, read as a trend
Assign each probe a lane with the `lane` field. Putting a probe in lane 1 is
usually wrong: lane 1 is for things only a person can resolve.
title: Acme Ops — Cognitive Load Dashboard

$comment: A markdown file whose headings are the queue. Heading shape:
## <severity marker> [<topic>] <title>
An item is raised to lane 1 when it is urgent, OR when it names a decision and is
neither waiting on someone else nor already resolved.
The two suppressions are NOT applied to critical/high items — mistaking 'our move'
for 'waiting on them' silently parks real work, so this errs toward over-surfacing.

probes.label: Open PRs
probes.$comment: Omit `owners` to use the current repository's owner. `limit` guards against gh's default 30-item truncation — the page announces when a query was cut off.

probes.label: Endpoints up
probes.$comment: Status codes only. A 200 is not evidence the response body is correct.

probes.label: Routines due
$comment: Generic escape hatch: counts non-empty output lines. A non-zero exit renders UNKNOWN rather than 0.
PREFER `count_pattern` over line counting whenever the tool prints its own total.
Counting lines breaks the moment the tool prints anything else — a footer, or a
'nothing due' notice on the empty day, which then counts as ONE item. If the tool
emits a summary line, read it with one capture group instead:
"count_pattern": "due ([0-9]+)/[0-9]+"
WARNING about `ok_exit_codes`: only widen it when the tool genuinely signals findings
with a non-zero exit (grep-style). If the tool always exits 0 when healthy, listing 1
as acceptable turns a CRASH into a confident '0 items' — the exact silent-zero this
dashboard exists to prevent. When unsure, leave it at [0].

probes.label: Loop spend
probes.$comment: When unknown_key reaches denominator_key, the value renders UNKNOWN instead of its literal (usually 0) value — an unmeasured cost must not read as a free one.

probes.label: ADRs
probes.$comment: An empty match renders UNKNOWN, not 0: naming conventions drift silently and a confident zero is the worst possible output.
